name: freetoken
description: A mod handle on FreeToken — the edge-native Mixture-of-Experts serving engine that runs frontier open-weight models on one consumer GPU by keeping the experts in host RAM and streaming or computing them as the machine's bandwidth dictates. The engine needs Linux, an NVIDIA card on r580+ and CUDA 13; this module needs none of that, because its whole client half is stdlib over HTTP and the box with the GPU is almost never the box you are sitting at. So it does both halves honestly: on a machine that qualifies it reports the preflight line by line, installs ft into a venv of its own (those torch and kernel pins belong nowhere near a shared environment), and supervises ft serve with a pidfile and a log. On a machine that does not, it registers the ones that do — the serve port for inference, the control-daemon port for starting and switching models — and drives them from here. Anything it can read from the engine rather than guess, it reads: the served model name comes from /v1/models, the pool table from /v1/cache/status, the bandwidth profile that chose offload over hybrid from the daemon. Then it re-serves the fleet one stable base_url on :50660 that speaks both OpenAI and Anthropic, streaming passed through chunk for chunk, so anything holding a base_url can point at a gaming PC instead of a vendor while the engine behind it moves between machines and models.

wraps.cite: Yang et al., FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution, arXiv:2608.16157 (2026)
wraps.how: installed on demand into ~/.mod/freetoken/venv, or reached over HTTP where it already runs

frontend: src/app.py (stdlib — the console at /freetoken on :50661; proxies /freetoken/_api)
state: ~/.mod/freetoken — boxes.json (0600, may hold a daemon token), logs/, venv/, models/. Nothing private is ever written into this repo.

engine_requirements.gpu: NVIDIA, driver r580+ (native support for RTX 30/40/50)
engine_requirements.cuda: 13, with nvcc on PATH — kernels are JIT-compiled on first use
engine_requirements.note: none of these are required to USE this module against a remote engine

ports_upstream.daemon: 1900 — ft daemon: /engine/start|stop|switch|status|logs|metrics, /bench/*, /checkpoint/*; X-FT-Token when started with --token

moe_backends.auto: dense → fused; MoE → offload, upgraded to hybrid when a cached bench profile recommends it
moe_backends.fused: experts resident on the GPU — needs the VRAM, never auto-selected
moe_backends.offload: experts in host RAM, an LRU cache of expert slots on the GPU; misses stream over PCIe
moe_backends.cpu: misses are computed on the CPU instead of fetched
moe_backends.hybrid: fetch some misses over PCIe, compute the rest on CPU, overlapped — calibrated by ft bench bw

endpoints.provider: GET /v1/models | POST /v1/chat/completions | POST /v1/completions | POST /v1/messages | POST /v1/messages/count_tokens | POST /v1/responses

env.FREETOKEN_MODELS: colon-separated extra directories to scan for checkpoints
env.HF_HOME: where the Hugging Face cache is scanned from
